routes.label: Use the logarithm as an exponent

question: If \(a\gt1,\) \(b\gt1\) and \(p=\frac{\log_b(\log_ba)}{\log_ba},\) then \(a^p\) equals
solution:
The expression \(\log_b a\) appears twice, so let
\[
t=\log_b a.
\]
Since \(a>1\) and \(b>1\), we have \(t>0\). Thus \(\log_b t\) is defined and division by \(t\) is allowed. The definition of a logarithm gives \(a=b^t\), while the given expression becomes \(p=(\log_b t)/t\). Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
a^p
&=(b^t)^{\frac{\log_b t}{t}}\\
&=b^{\log_b t}\\
&=t.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last equality follows because exponentiation with base \(b\) reverses taking a logarithm with base \(b\). Hence \(\boxed{a^p=\log_b a}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
